around.headline: Two men posing as prospective tenants rob Bengaluru woman of gold
around.summary: Two men called about a room for rent, asked to view it in person, and made off with the woman's gold while she was distracted showing them around. If you're renting out a room or PG, never leave visitors unsupervised near cash or jewellery — lock valuables away before anyone steps inside.

around.headline: Search intensifies for Bengaluru techie missing on a solo trek at Shivagange
around.summary: A 31-year-old techie has been missing since trekking alone at Shivagange Hills; his bike was found at the foothills but his phone last pinged elsewhere, and search teams are still out. If you're planning a solo trek this weekend, share your live location with someone and stick to marked trails.
around.source: The New Indian Express, Times of India

around.headline: Bengaluru set to tighten traffic rules
around.summary: City authorities are rolling out stricter traffic enforcement, with more checks expected on common violations. Budget a little extra caution (and time) on your commute over the next few days while the new rules bed in.

around.headline: Metro Purple Line suspended for 2 hours; metal sheet falls near Kadubeesanahalli station
around.summary: Purple Line services were halted for about two hours, and separately a metal sheet from ongoing metro construction fell onto the road near Kadubeesanahalli station. If your route passes active metro construction, give barricaded stretches a wider berth, especially in this rain.

around.headline: Third day of hotel raids: over 100kg of expired food seized in Bengaluru
around.summary: FDA raids on 3-star and 5-star hotels have now run three days straight, turning up expired meat, fungal vegetables and poor hygiene, with over 100kg of food seized and discarded. A hotel's star rating isn't a hygiene guarantee — check for visible cleanliness and fresh stock even at premium outlets.

around.headline: Oil prices rise on uncertainty over Strait of Hormuz reopening
around.summary: Crude prices ticked up amid uncertainty about the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil shipping route, even as the US signals a more low-key approach on Iran. Sustained higher crude tends to feed into petrol/diesel prices here with a lag, so it's worth watching if you're budgeting for fuel.

street_smart.title: Two strangers call about the room you've listed for rent and want to see it right now — one asks you to "stay with them" in the room so they don't waste time going back and forth, while you're home alone. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru incident: two men posing as prospective tenants distracted a woman during a room viewing and stole her gold (Times of India).
street_smart.situation: Two well-dressed visitors show up to view a room you've listed for rent. You're home alone and it's just the three of you.

choices.text: Let them in, then step into the kitchen to make tea while they look around the room on their own.
choices.feedback: This is exactly the trap that worked today: stepping away to be a good host hands visitors a few unsupervised minutes near your cupboards, jewellery box, or wherever cash is kept. Politeness shouldn't come before supervision.

choices.text: Lock away cash, jewellery and documents before the visit, and stay in the room with both visitors the entire time.
choices.feedback: Correct. Removing valuables from the room before anyone arrives means there's nothing to steal even if you're momentarily distracted, and staying present the whole time removes the unsupervised window a distraction scam depends on.

choices.text: Ask for a photo ID copy after the viewing, then let them wander the house alone to "compare" other rooms.
choices.feedback: An ID copy collected after the fact doesn't protect anything during the visit, and letting visitors roam unsupervised — even briefly — is the actual point of failure, regardless of what paperwork you have on file.

choices.text: Agree to show the room, but only after asking them to come back with a broker or when a neighbour is around.
choices.feedback: Better than nothing, but it's not always practical to postpone every viewing, and it doesn't teach the actual safeguard: never let a visitor roam unsupervised near valuables, broker or no broker.

takeaways: Lock away cash, jewellery and important documents before any home viewing — tenant, repairman, or delivery agent — so there's nothing to steal even if you're distracted.
Never leave a visitor unsupervised inside your home, even for a minute to make tea or take a call.
Ask for a phone number and photo ID before the visit (not after), and share those details with a family member or neighbour so someone else knows who's in your home.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's ongoing hotel raids this week turned up which food safety issue at several 3-star and 5-star hotels?
quiz.why: Inspectors seized over 100kg of expired meat, sauces and fungal vegetables by the third day of raids — a reminder that a hotel's star rating says nothing about kitchen hygiene.

quiz.question: Namma Metro's Purple Line services were suspended for roughly how long recently?
quiz.why: BMRCL typically posts real-time disruption updates on its app and social media, worth a quick check before you head to the station.

quiz.question: Oil prices have been rising on uncertainty around the reopening of which key shipping route?
quiz.why: The Strait of Hormuz, between the Persian Gulf and the open ocean, is a chokepoint for roughly a fifth of the world's oil shipments, so disruption risk there moves global crude prices.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age to be eligible to vote in India?
quiz.why: The 61st Constitutional Amendment in 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18.

quiz.question: Nandi Hills, a popular weekend trekking spot near Bengaluru, is part of which hill range?
quiz.why: Nandi Hills sits at the northern edge of the Eastern Ghats' extension into the Deccan Plateau, distinct from the Western Ghats that run along India's west coast.
